overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA) adjudicates requests for variances, special permits, and Chapter 40B comprehensive permits within the city. Meeting from May 2024 through September 2026, the board oversaw residential expansions, commercial use changes, and large-scale housing developments while ensuring compliance with local and state zoning regulations. The body frequently coordinates with city departments and peer consultants regarding traffic mitigation, flood prevention, and stormwater management. As of the most recent meeting, the board is actively grappling with the interpretation of new state guidelines regarding Accessory Dwelling Units while managing a steady volume of residential relief petitions.

threads.name: 970 Fellsway Chapter 40B Development
threads.summary: The board conducted an extensive review of a proposed 289-unit housing development, focusing on civil engineering, traffic peer studies, and site circulation (M01#2, M01#6). A significant portion of the deliberation involved whether market-rate units were subject to the city's linkage ordinance, which the board eventually affirmed (M03#2). The comprehensive permit was approved in May 2024 with a partial linkage fee waiver granted in exchange for off-site public improvements (M04#3). A subsequent special permit was granted to facilitate a lot split for the project while preserving an existing commercial structure (M11#2).

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs)
threads.summary: Starting in mid-2026, the board began reviewing petitions for Accessory Dwelling Units under updated state zoning regulations (M19#3, M19#6). While some simple ADU setbacks were approved, complex petitions involving attic expansions on Vassar Street and Wellesley Street faced multiple continuances (M19#4, M20#1). The board has delayed final decisions on these cases to seek further legal counsel and wait for modified designs that better align with state guidelines (M21#1, M21#2).

threads.name: Cannabis Dispensary Permitting
threads.summary: The board processed multiple special permit requests for an adult-use and medical cannabis dispensary at 114 Mystic Avenue (M17#2). Initial approvals were granted for medical sales and product manufacturing, though a request for delivery services was initially delayed for police input (M17#2). After further review by legal counsel, the board approved the special permit for cannabis delivery in July 2026 (M18#1, M19#1).

threads.name: Board Governance and Membership
threads.summary: The board has undergone several leadership and administrative changes, including the resignation of chair Jamie Thompson and the election of Mike Caldera as his successor (M12#3, M13#1). Members have consistently worked on updating the board's dated rules and regulations while managing a backlog of meeting minutes using new transcription software (M06#3, M10#3, M14#8). Throughout 2025 and 2026, the board monitored the status of new member appointments from the Mayor's office to ensure consistent voting quorums (M15#4, M16#2).

threads.name: Commercial and Mixed-Use Conversions
threads.summary: The board frequently evaluates petitions to convert non-conforming commercial spaces into residential or community uses. Examples include the conversion of a first-floor commercial unit on Main Street into a residence and a real estate office on Boston Avenue into a community cafe (M11#4, M18#8). Other projects involved mixed-use renovations for a play cafe and an aesthetic spa (M17#3, M21#4).

threads.name: Flood Mitigation and Topographical Relief
threads.summary: Zoning relief is often requested to address chronic flooding issues caused by Medford's topography. The board approved variances to infill below-grade garages and driveways to prevent flooding on Lincoln Street and Judkins Road (M07#4, M09#1). In several cases, the board conditioned approvals on the use of permeable pavers or specific stormwater management plans to mitigate neighborhood drainage impacts (M15#1, M20#2).

threads.name: Chapter 40B Major Project Oversight
threads.summary: Beyond the Fellsway project, the board monitors other large 40B developments, such as a 350-unit project at 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway (M09#2). In that case, the board determined that design refinements regarding amenity locations and trash rooms were insubstantial changes (M09#2). Conversely, the board accepted the withdrawal of a 378-unit multi-family petition on Mystic Avenue and continued a separate case due to a non-responsive applicant (M04#2, M05#2).

periods.narrative: This period was dominated by the review and approval of the 970 Fellsway Chapter 40B project and several smaller residential variances for porches and additions.
During this term, the board focused on cannabis dispensary delivery permits and the initial local implementation of state-mandated Accessory Dwelling Unit regulations.
